\begin{proof}
Let
\[
f(x)=\frac{(x+2)^p-2^p}{x}.
\]
The numerator has zero constant term, so $f\in\mathbb Z[x]$. Expanding gives
\[
f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{p}\binom pj2^{p-j}x^{j-1}.
\]
Its leading coefficient is $1$. For $1\le j\le p-1$, the primality of $p$ implies $p\mid\binom pj$, so $p$ divides every nonleading coefficient. Its constant coefficient is $p2^{p-1}$, and since $p$ is odd, $p\nmid2$, hence $p^2\nmid p2^{p-1}$. Eisenstein's criterion therefore implies that $f$ is irreducible over $\mathbb Q$, and, being monic with integer coefficients, it is irreducible in $\mathbb Z[x]$.
\end{proof}
